newsitem.title: UK: Precious metals listless in range-bound London.
newsitem.headline: Precious metals listless in range-bound London.

text.p: The precious metals were subdued and prices remained narrowly rangebound on Tuesday afternoon as gold nervously eyed Wall Street and other markets for direction.
"Right now this market is taking its lead from other markets, namely equities, bonds and the dollar," a dealer said.

Bullion fixed at $323.45 in the afternoon, compared to $322.10 in the morning, after starting the week above $326.00. Physical offtake around $322 an ounce has emerged, underpinning the otherwise jittery, bearish market.
A plunge in U.S. stocks last Friday had resulted in only mild gains for gold, all of which were erased on Monday after the Dow's recovery.
Shortly after the gold fixing Wall Street stocks were firmer in early steady trading after a sharp 108-point rise late on Monday and the dollar was steady.
The market was also watching for results of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting, due around 1815 GMT. However, no change in U.S. interest rates was expected.
Rumours that a central bank selling its gold reserves was behind gold's sharp decline on Monday were also swirling around the market.
"Talk of central bank selling is at the forefront again. But it's all conjecture at this point -- you won't know until it's happened," a dealer said.

In the other precious metals, silver was trading in a tiny range just above $4.50 an ounce -- the centre of its recent price range. It was last quoted one cent firmer than at Monday's London close, at $4.52/$4.54.
"Silver is holding up amazingly well. People are trying to sell it but it's being absorbed," a dealer said.
But recent weakness in copper, which has lost six percent of its value since last Thursday, may leak over into silver, which is frequently mined with the red metal.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) continued to ease steadily, against a background of greater liquidity as Russian material trickled onto the market.
However, palladium found some interim support at the psychological $200 level.
It was last stradding the figure at $198.00/$203.00, compared to Monday's closing $206.25/$209.25.
